title: Scan open TCP ports on a host using netcat
summary: Use netcat to check which TCP ports are open on a remote host. This is useful for basic network troubleshooting or security checks.

steps.explain: Use netcat in verbose mode (-v) to scan a range of ports on a target host. The -z flag tells netcat to scan without sending data, and -w sets a timeout for each connection attempt.

placeholders.name: TIMEOUT
placeholders.description: Timeout in seconds for each connection attempt

placeholders.name: HOST
placeholders.description: The IP address or hostname to scan

placeholders.description: The first port number in the range
